claims.text: Al0.6TiCrFeCoNi coatings can be deposited on a steel substrate by HVOF thermal spraying.
The proposed HEA coatings possess a multiphase BCC/FCC microstructure with high hardness and strain-hardening capability.
At ambient bulk temperature, HEA-coating tribological performance is dominated by competition between strain hardening and formation of a protective tribo-oxide layer.
Sluggish diffusion and lattice distortion cause the relevant strain hardening.
At low normal loads, stable and hard Cr2O3 or TiO2 tribo-films form on the coating.
The protective oxide film reduces the coefficient of friction and produces high wear resistance.
Increasing sliding velocity or normal load raises the local flash temperature through frictional heating.
The QA parameter provides a method for quantifying frictional heating power per unit time and unit area.
The QA parameter directly provides the local flash temperature used to identify the degradation boundary.
Higher normal load promotes adhered contact-surface fragments and increased friction.
Exceeding the oxide-layer stability limit causes a transition from mild oxidative wear to severe adhesive wear.
Thermally activated plasticity, dynamic recovery, or phase instability in the coating's BCC/FCC phases causes thermal softening.
Wear performance of an Al0.6TiCrFeCoNi coating on ASTM A572 steel has been evaluated over 300 to 500 °C.
High configurational entropy delays coating softening relative to conventional alloys.
Wear rate remains low and stable while local flash temperature is below 300 °C.
Wear rate increases sharply when local flash temperature reaches approximately 400 to 500 °C.
The coefficient of friction first decreases during oxide formation and then increases when adhesive wear dominates.
At a normal load of 20 N, performance degrades when sliding velocity exceeds 3 m/s.
Conventional NiCrBSi coatings show a more linear increase in wear rate with temperature or velocity because they have lower strain hardening and less stable oxide layers.
The degradation threshold depends on alloy composition and substrate thermal conductivity because these affect oxide stability and heat dissipation.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome specifies a sharp wear-rate increase, whereas the uncertainty field states that the transition may be gradual rather than abrupt.
